The firearms were found in Keith's vehicle on Davis Road during a traffic stop, not at the alleged trafficking location (apartment). Officer Perry perjured himself before the grand jury as the ONLY officer to place firearms at the apartment. Without the "in furtherance" nexus, the firearm aggravator fails and the Class A charge is legally unsupported. DISCOVERED: Attorney Intake Memo / grand jury analysis, Oct 2025.

These are irreconcilably contradictory statements under a legally binding FOAA obligation. A false statement in an FOAA response violates 1 M.R.S.A. § 408-A. violations.violation_type: Fair Housing Act § 3617 Retaliation — Housing Revoked Within Days of FOAA Request About 2018 Incident
violations.description: August 2024: Brewer Housing Authority (BrHA) approved Keith's housing application. Staff member Aaliyah verbally assured Keith that his background check issues were 'not a concern.' Keith was placed at the TOP of the waiting list for 2- and 3-bedroom apartments at Norumbega. An apartment was assigned with a move-in date. 2-3 days AFTER Keith submitted a FOAA request to Joe Knox (BHA) requesting 2018 incident records, BrHA revoked the housing approval -- citing the same '$600 debt and criminal history' that Aaliyah had already said was not a concern. The Fair Housing Act prohibits retaliation against persons who exercise fair housing rights or file complaints (42 U.S.C. § 3617). Filing a FOAA request about police misconduct in public housing is a protected activity. Revoking housing 2-3 days after that request constitutes retaliation. SOURCE: Keith FOIA/FOAA request Aug 3, 2025 and prior BrHA approval/revocation documentation.
violations.law_reference: 42 U.S.C. § 3617 (FHA Anti-Retaliation); 24 C.F.R. § 100.400; 42 U.S.C. § 3604 (FHA); Maine Human Rights Act
